tldr: International headlines uniformly lead with the livestreamed murder-suicide as a crime event, foregrounding the act and the medium. Philippine domestic headlines diverge sharply — none of the three lead with the killing itself; instead they add disputed motive, media restraint, and civic mourning, frames invisible to the global headline reader.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to use 'terror' language, framing the shooting as a horror spectacle rather than a discrete crime; also the only title to name Facebook explicitly as the broadcast platform.
Only headline to contextualise the shooting as a recurring national pattern — 'second school shooting in two months' — adding a systemic dimension absent from all other international titles.

Headline ('US tourist killed by lightning strike on Mount Etna during hike in restricted area') is for an unrelated story and appears misassigned to this cluster; the uk bucket's on-topic coverage comes solely from The Guardian.

bottom_line: Outside the Philippines, every headline reduces this event to a crime spectacle — 'kills,' 'killed,' 'school shooting' — while Philippine outlets alone surface the questions of motive, mental health, and media responsibility that will shape domestic policy response.
